pl-l2d25c5-d1e108.summary: States that the first freedom of choice was greater than the second, and the third much greater than both: the first could sin and not sin; the last will be able not to sin and unable to sin; the middle can sin and cannot not sin, before restoration even mortally, after restoration at least venially.
claims: Freedom has three stages of increasing perfection.
In the present state man cannot avoid all sin.

pl-l2d25c5.summary: Concludes that the first freedom of choice was greater than the second, and the third far greater than both: the first could sin and not sin; the last will be able not to sin and unable to sin; the middle can sin and cannot not sin, before restoration even mortally, after restoration at least venially.
claims: The first freedom: able to sin and not to sin.
The middle freedom: able to sin and unable not to sin.
The final freedom: able not to sin and unable to sin.
Before restoration man cannot avoid mortal sin; after, he cannot avoid venial sin.
